oneLine: Turns a shift's forecast volume into a plan, then releases work to the floor continuously, earliest cut-off first. It watches backlog and flags where to rebalance.

rows.title: Record the volume due by each cut-off
rows.story: A planner records how many units are due by each carrier cut-off for a path. For case picks, the cases, cube and weight are worked out from the SKU's pack facts.

rows.title: Commit the plan for a path
rows.story: A planner commits rate, heads and hours for a path. Heads cannot exceed the stations installed. If workforce-management has already committed a different headcount, the difference is flagged in the same step.

rows.title: Compare with the labour plan
rows.story: workforce-management commits its own headcount per path. This service keeps a read-only copy and, if its own plan for the path has different heads, flags the difference. It only flags; neither plan is corrected.
rows.policy: Whenever the labour plan arrives, keep a copy and flag a difference in heads from our plan

rows.title: Turn an allocated order into work
rows.story: When an order is allocated, fully or in part, each released line becomes one work unit on its process path. A path the catalogue does not know is refused loudly instead of filling a pool nobody serves.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is allocated, enqueue one work unit per released line

then.does: confirms the order line was released to the floor planner, so it knows nothing was lost

rows.title: Turn a stock transfer into work
rows.story: network-inventory-planning releases a transfer demand. It becomes one work unit named after the demand, so a repeat of the same demand never makes a second one. Only transfer legs are accepted, never relocation.
rows.policy: Whenever a transfer demand is released, enqueue one work unit for it

rows.title: Turn an approved slot plan into relocation work
rows.story: slotting-optimization approves a plan of moves. Each move becomes a relocation unit, and a move waiting on another stays blocked until that one completes. A newer plan cancels the older plan's unreleased moves.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot plan is approved, plan one relocation unit per move and cancel older unreleased moves

rows.title: Turn a pick-face top-up request into work
rows.story: pick-face-replenishment asks for a top-up, and it becomes one work unit, urgent ones sorting ahead. A cancellation before release withdraws the unit. Work already released runs to completion.
rows.policy: Whenever a top-up is requested, plan one work unit for it, with a deadline set by its priority

rows.title: Release the next work
rows.story: A supervisor, or an agent, releases the pending work unit with the earliest cut-off. A path fed by release stops at its work-in-progress limit. The release carries hazard hints from the product's classification.

then.does: turns the released work into a floor task needing the skills its path requires

rows.title: Finish a work unit when its task is done
rows.story: When the floor completes the task, the work unit is completed and its slot in the pool is freed. A completed relocation admits the moves that were waiting behind it. Tasks this service never planned are ignored.
rows.policy: Whenever a floor task completes, complete its work unit and free its work-in-progress slot

rows.title: Watch a path's backlog
rows.story: A supervisor samples a path's backlog. Over its alarm threshold, an alarm goes out. If a cut-off time is given, the path's remaining room for new work before it is announced too.

then.does: opens or updates an exception for the path on a backlog alarm
keeps the remaining room per path and cut-off for its delivery promises
keeps the remaining room per path for its own capacity figures

rows.title: Decide how to rebalance a path
rows.story: A supervisor asks what to do about a path. A flow-fed path over its alarm gets 'throttle upstream'. A release-fed path stuck at its limit with work waiting gets 'reassign labour'. Both are flags only. A rate deviation notice is declared but never raised.

rows.title: Set how a path's pool is fed
rows.story: A supervisor sets whether a path is fed by release or by flow, and its work-in-progress limit. Lowering the limit never evicts work: releases just pause until the count falls under it. Nothing is announced.

rows.title: Keep the process-path list
rows.story: process-path-management announces every path defined, revised or retired. When the catalogue source is set to that feed, this service follows it live. By default it reads a file instead.
rows.policy: Whenever a path is created, revised or retired, update the local process-path list

rows.title: Keep the product hazard and pack facts
rows.story: product-master announces each product's classification, such as hazmat or fragile, and its pack levels. This service keeps its own copies and stamps the hints on released work. A newer version replaces an older one.
rows.policy: Whenever a product is classified or its pack level changes, replace the local copy with the newer version

rows.title: Keep the usable-stock view
rows.story: inventory-storage announces stock reserved and reservations revoked. This service keeps a read-only count of usable stock per SKU that operators can look up. No release decision depends on it.
rows.policy: Whenever stock is reserved or a reservation is revoked, adjust the usable-stock count for that SKU

rows.title: Feed the throughput report
rows.story: The service reads its own announcements and keeps hourly figures per path: work released and completed, backlog alarms and throttling. They feed the release throughput report.
rows.policy: Whenever work is released or completed, or an alarm is raised, add it to that path's hourly figures

hotspots.text: RateDeviationDetected is declared but no rule raises it. A test fails if code starts raising it before a decision defines when.
PathPlanDriftDetected has no reader yet. Any reaction by another context, such as an alert, is explicitly deferred.
Remaining room for flow-fed paths is permanently unknown, and a consumer must match it to a cut-off by nearest time because there is no stronger key.
Committing a plan can ask facility-layout live for a travel distance. It is optional and fails open. Moving it to events is a tracked follow-up.

opportunities.text: A real-time, sub-hour observed-throughput figure per flow-fed path is deferred until a consumer needs fresher data than the report.
A cancellation event for unreleased work units can be added if a consumer needs one. Today a cancelled unit is visible only through the read API.
Drift detection could also compare rate and hours, and track drift across shifts. Today it compares planned heads only.
